title: Experiment: enterprise access packaging & contract commitments for SSO/SAML and RBAC
creator: Hana Li
description:
Background: Sales and Legal have asked for clearer, testable packaging options that map specific enterprise access controls (IdP-based SSO/SAML assertions and role-based access controls) to contractual commitments. Right now we verbally promise support for SSO and RBAC in enterprise deals, but the lack of a standardized commitment matrix slows negotiations and leaks variability into price and support effort.

Goal: Run an experiment to (1) define a packaging axis that ties discrete contractual commitments for SSO/SAML and RBAC to pricing tiers, (2) pilot contract language and questionnaire templates, and (3) measure impact on sales velocity, close rate, and post-sale support tickets.

Scope: Packaging will include three offer levels for access controls: "Essentials" (self-serve SSO guidance, no SLA), "Managed Access" (SAML setup assistance, basic RBAC role templates, 30-day remediation SLA), and "Committed Access" (onboarding assistance, SAML assertion verification, fine-grained RBAC in product, 99% availability commitment and defined escalation SLA). The experiment covers new incoming enterprise opportunities over an 8-week pilot.

Deliverables: standardized commitment matrix (CSV/Confluence), contract addendum language snippets for each tier, security questionnaire answers and RACI for pre-sale verifications, a pilot pricing sheet, and a feedback loop with Sales/Legal/Support.

Success metrics: conversion rate from opportunity to signed contract (+/- baseline), average time-to-close, number of support incidents related to access control in first 90 days, Legal review iterations per contract, and NPS of early customers on onboarding.

Risks & mitigations: (1) Overpromising operational SLAs -> mitigate by defining explicit conditions and fallbacks; (2) Increased support burden for lower tiers -> mitigate with automated KB and checklist; (3) Security approval delays -> mitigate by pre-submitting standard questionnaire answers and having an assigned security reviewer.

Approach: 1) Draft commitment matrix and addendum (PM + Legal), 2) Align with Security for questionnaire answers and bake any non-functional requirements into the product acceptance criteria, 3) Train Sales on the new tiers and run a short pilot of 10–15 opportunities, 4) Track outcomes and iterate.

Stakeholders: PM (Hana Li), Sales Lead (Priya Rao), Legal (Ethan Morales), Security (Nina Feldman), Support Lead (Jamal Ortiz), Engineering contacts for RBAC onboarding (Marcus Chen).

Artifacts: Confluence draft (https://confluence.redwood.com/enterprise-access-packaging), pricing sheet draft (Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake/pricing-sheet), sample contract addendum PR (https://github.com/redwood/contracts/pull/312).
acceptance_criteria: Commitment matrix doc published in Confluence with clear definitions and operational bounds for each tier
Three contract addendum templates (one per tier) reviewed and provisionally approved by Legal
Completed security questionnaire answers and assigned security reviewer confirmed
Sales enablement materials (one-pager + playbook) created and training session scheduled
Pilot run started with at least 8 qualified opportunities and tracking dashboard capturing KPIs
